# 12-Week Bodyweight Strength Programme

**Client profile:** 27 years old, beginner, training at home
**Equipment:** Yoga mat, doorway pull-up bar
**Frequency:** 3 sessions per week (Mon / Wed / Fri), with optional mobility on off days
**Session length:** approximately 45–60 minutes

Because the equipment is limited, progression relies on leverage changes, tempo, unilateral variations, pause reps, and volume rather than added load. Before starting, check the doorway bar is rated for body weight and mounted securely into the frame, and that the client has room to swing without hitting walls or furniture.

---

## Phase 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–4)

**Goal:** Build movement competency, joint readiness, and baseline work capacity. Emphasis on controlled technique and learning the pulling and pushing patterns.

**Weekly structure:** Each session follows the same template: a 5-minute warm-up, the main strength circuit, and a 5-minute cool-down. Rest 60–90 seconds between sets.

**Warm-up (every session):** 2 minutes of jumping jacks or marching in place, 10 arm circles each direction, 10 bodyweight squats, 10 scapular pull-downs on the bar (hanging, shoulders depressed), 5 inchworms.

### Week 1
- **Session A (Mon):** Incline push-ups (hands on a sturdy table or sofa arm) 3×8; Bodyweight squats 3×12; Glute bridges 3×12; Dead hangs from bar 3×15–20 seconds; Plank 3×20 seconds
- **Session B (Wed):** Negative pull-ups (jump to top, lower over 4 seconds) 3×3; Reverse lunges 3×8 per leg; Split squat hold on wall 3×20 seconds per leg; Superman holds 3×15 seconds; Dead bug 3×8 per side
- **Session C (Fri):** Pike push-ups on the mat 3×6; Single-leg glute bridges 3×8 per leg; Wall sit 3×30 seconds; Bird dogs 3×8 per side; Hollow body hold (tuck variation) 3×15 seconds

### Week 2
Repeat Week 1 structure with progression: add 2 reps to push-ups and squats, increase hangs to 25 seconds, and extend the negative pull-up lowering to 5 seconds.

### Week 3
- **Session A:** Standard push-ups 3×6 (or incline if not yet able); Goblet-style squat holding a backpack loaded with books 3×12; Glute bridge march 3×10 per side; Dead hangs 3×25 seconds; Plank 3×30 seconds
- **Session B:** Band-free australian (inverted) rows under a sturdy table, or towel rows if no table; Reverse lunges 3×10 per leg; Single-leg Romanian deadlift (bodyweight) 3×8 per leg; Hollow body hold 3×20 seconds; Side plank 3×20 seconds per side
- **Session C:** Pike push-ups 3×8; Bulgarian split squat (rear foot on sofa) 3×8 per leg; Wall sit 3×45 seconds; Dead bug 3×10 per side; Hanging knee raises 3×8

### Week 4
Deload-light week. Reduce total sets by one per exercise and keep reps the same. Focus on perfect form and record baseline numbers: max push-ups, max strict pull-ups, max single-leg squats, plank time. Use these as benchmarks for Phase 2.

---

## Phase 2: Build (Weeks 5–8)

**Goal:** Increase strength through harder leverages, slower tempos, and unilateral loading.

**Warm-up:** Same as Phase 1, plus 5 scapular pull-ups before the main work.

### Week 5
- **Session A:** Decline push-ups (feet on sofa) 4×8; Pistol squat progression (box squat to a chair, 3 sets of 5 per leg); Nordic hamstring negatives (kneeling, anchored feet) 3×4; Hollow body hold 3×30 seconds; Pallof-style towel press (anchor towel to door) 3×10 per side
- **Session B:** Pull-ups (full range if able, otherwise negatives 4×4 at 5-second lowering); Bulgarian split squat 3×10 per leg; Single-leg RDL 3×10 per leg; Australian rows with feet elevated 4×10; Dragon-flag progression (tuck to half) 3×5
- **Session C:** Diamond push-ups 3×8; Jump squats 3×10; Single-leg glute bridge with 3-second hold 3×12 per leg; Wall handstand hold (hands on floor, feet on wall, hold 20 seconds) 3×20 seconds; Hanging leg raises 3×10

### Week 6
Increase volume: add one set to each main exercise. Pull-ups progress to 4×5 if full reps achieved, or continue negatives at 6-second lowering. Pistol squat progression advances to box height lowered by one step.

### Week 7
- **Session A:** Pseudo-planche push-ups (hands by hips, lean forward) 4×6; Pistol squat to lower box 3×5 per leg; Nordic curls (full or assisted) 4×4; Hollow body rocks 3×12; Towel-anchored single-arm row (anchored at door) 3×10 per side
- **Session B:** Weighted-free pull-up variations: chin-ups 4×6, wide-grip pull-ups 3×5; Shrimp squats 3×6 per leg; Single-leg hip thrust on sofa 3×12 per leg; Front lever tuck holds 3×15 seconds; L-sit on floor between chairs 3×15 seconds
- **Session C:** Archer push-ups 3×5 per side; Jump lunges 3×10 per leg; Handstand push-up negatives against wall 4×3 (lower slowly, 5 seconds); Dead bug with hold 3×12; Hanging knee-to-elbow 3×8

### Week 8
Test week. Retest the Week 4 benchmarks plus a 60-second max-rep set of each: push-ups, pull-ups, and bodyweight squats. Record and compare.

---

## Phase 3: Peak (Weeks 9–12)

**Goal:** Consolidate strength gains, add density and skill work, and finish with a strong performance test.

**Warm-up:** Same as Phase 2, plus 2 minutes of light shadow boxing or skipping.

### Week 9
- **Session A:** Full push-up variations: standard 4×10; Archer push-ups 3×6 per side; Pike push-ups elevated on sofa 3×8; Hollow body hold 3×40 seconds; Plank with shoulder taps 3×20 per side
- **Session B:** Pull-ups 5×6 (or negatives if not yet able); Pistol squat 3×6 per leg (full depth if achieved); Nordic curls 4×5; Single-arm towel row 3×10 per side; Front lever tuck holds 3×20 seconds
- **Session C:** Handstand push-up negatives 4×4; Jump lunges 3×12; Single-leg hip thrust 3×15 per leg; L-sit 3×20 seconds; Hanging leg raises 3×12

### Week 10
Density block. Perform each session as a circuit: complete all exercises in order, rest 90 seconds, repeat for 3 rounds. Aim to match or exceed Week 9 rep totals each round.

### Week 11
Skill emphasis. Session A: practise full-range pistol squats and handstand holds for skill, keeping sets low (3×3) and quality high. Session B: pull-up volume at 5×5 with 2-minute rests. Session C: archer push-up and L-sit progressions for 4 sets each. Keep Nordic curls and hollow holds in all sessions.

### Week 12
Final test. Retest all benchmarks: max push-ups, max strict pull-ups, max pistol squats per leg, max handstand hold, plank, and hollow hold. Compare to Week 4 baseline and document the change.

---

## Nutrition and Recovery Guidance

- **Protein:** Roughly 1.6–2.0 g per kg of body weight daily, spread across 3–4 meals.
- **Calories:** Maintain or slightly exceed maintenance if the goal is strength and muscle gain. Adjust weekly based on bodyweight trend.
- **Sleep:** 7–9 hours. This is the single largest recovery lever.
- **Hydration:** Around 35 ml per kg of body weight daily, more on training days.
- **Rest days:** Thursday, Saturday, and Sunday. A 10–15 minute mobility routine (hip flexor stretches, thoracic rotations, hamstring and calf stretches) is recommended on these days.
- **Soreness:** Mild soreness in the first two weeks is normal. Sharp joint pain, numbness, or pain that worsens over sessions should prompt a reduction in load or a medical check.

## Coaching Notes for the Remote Trainer

- Request a short video of each exercise in week 1 to check form remotely.
- Ask the client to log reps, RPE (1–10), and any pain after each session.
- Progress only when the client completes all prescribed sets with good form and RPE 8 or below. If not, repeat the week.
- Confirm the client has a clear floor area and no fragile ceilings or light fittings near the bar.
- Screen for shoulder, elbow, or lower back issues before starting. Refer to a physiotherapist for any pre-existing injury.

# Nutrition Plan: 12-Week Strength Programme

**Client profile:** 27 years old, beginner, training 3× per week at home
**Goal:** Build strength and lean muscle while keeping body composition in check
**Important:** Calorie and macro targets below are starting estimates. Confirm his current bodyweight, height, activity level, and any dietary restrictions before finalising. Recalculate at Week 4 and Week 8 using his bodyweight trend.

---

## Step 1: Estimate Maintenance Calories

Without his stats, the following is a template. Once you have them, use this method:

1. **Estimate BMR** using the Mifflin-St Jeor equation:
   - Men: (10 × weight in kg) + (6.25 × height in cm) − (5 × age) + 5
2. **Multiply by an activity factor:**
   - Sedentary desk job, 3 sessions/week: BMR × 1.4
   - Lightly active with daily walking: BMR × 1.5
3. **Set the target:**
   - Muscle gain focus: maintenance + 200–300 kcal/day
   - Recomp (lose fat, keep muscle): maintenance − 200 kcal/day
   - Default for a beginner: maintenance + 250 kcal/day

Worked example for an 80 kg, 178 cm, 27-year-old man, desk-based: BMR ≈ 1,780 kcal; maintenance ≈ 2,490 kcal; muscle-gain target ≈ 2,750 kcal/day.

---

## Step 2: Macronutrient Targets

| Macro | Target | Example (80 kg client) |
|---|---|---|
| Protein | 1.8–2.2 g/kg | 150–175 g/day |
| Fat | 25–30% of calories | 0.8–1.0 g/kg (about 70–90 g) |
| Carbohydrates | Remainder of calories | About 330–370 g/day |

**Why these numbers:** Protein drives muscle repair and growth. Fat supports hormone production and should not drop below about 0.7 g/kg. Carbohydrates fuel training sessions and are best placed around workouts.

---

## Step 3: Meal Structure

Aim for 4 meals per day, each with a palm-sized or larger protein portion.

- **Breakfast:** 40 g protein, complex carbohydrate, fruit. Example: 3 eggs plus 2 eggs' worth of egg whites, two slices of wholegrain toast, a banana, and Greek yoghurt.
- **Lunch:** 40–45 g protein, rice or potatoes, vegetables, olive oil. Example: 150 g chicken breast, 200 g cooked rice, roasted vegetables, a drizzle of olive oil.
- **Pre-training snack (60–90 min before):** 20–30 g protein, 40–60 g carbohydrate. Example: oats with whey, or a bagel with tuna.
- **Dinner:** 40–45 g protein, carbohydrate source, vegetables. Example: 150 g salmon, 250 g potatoes, green beans.
- **Evening (optional, if short of protein):** 25–30 g casein or Greek yoghurt, or a cottage cheese bowl.

Training days can shift an extra 30–50 g of carbohydrate toward the pre-session snack. Rest days can trim carbs slightly and keep protein constant.

---

## Step 4: Hydration and Supplements

- **Water:** 35 ml/kg daily, plus 500 ml around each session.
- **Creatine monohydrate:** 3–5 g daily. Well supported for strength in beginners and low-cost. Recommend only after checking kidney function is normal and he has no medical contraindications.
- **Whey protein:** Useful only if he struggles to hit protein targets with whole foods.
- **Vitamin D:** Consider 1,000–2,000 IU daily in winter or if he has limited sun exposure. A blood test is the most reliable way to check.
- **Everything else:** Not necessary for this programme.

---

## Step 5: Weekly Adjustment Protocol

| Week | Action |
|---|---|
| 1–2 | Track food daily with an app. Log bodyweight every morning. |
| 3–4 | Review the 2-week average bodyweight. If gain is under 0.25 kg/week, add 150 kcal/day. If gain is over 0.5 kg/week, reduce by 150 kcal/day. |
| 5–8 | Repeat the same review every two weeks. |
| 9–12 | Hold intake steady unless bodyweight changes unexpectedly. Prioritise performance at test weeks. |

---

## Step 6: Sample Day (80 kg example, about 2,750 kcal, 165 g protein)

- **Breakfast:** Oats (80 g) cooked with 300 ml milk, 1 scoop whey, 1 banana, 20 g peanut butter. Approx. 650 kcal, 45 g protein.
- **Lunch:** 180 g chicken breast, 200 g cooked rice, mixed vegetables, 1 tbsp olive oil. Approx. 700 kcal, 50 g protein.
- **Pre-training:** 2 wholegrain rice cakes with 100 g tuna and a pear. Approx. 350 kcal, 30 g protein.
- **Dinner:** 170 g salmon, 250 g baked potatoes, broccoli, 1 tbsp butter. Approx. 750 kcal, 40 g protein.
- **Evening:** 200 g Greek yoghurt with 30 g granola and berries. Approx. 350 kcal, 20 g protein.

Total: roughly 2,800 kcal and 185 g protein. Trim rice or potato by 50 g if overshooting calories.

---

## Coaching Notes

- Screen for allergies, eating disorder history, kidney or liver conditions, and diabetes before setting targets. Refer to a registered dietitian for any of these.
- Avoid rigid restriction. Build meals from foods he enjoys and can repeat.
- Encourage consistent meal timing, but flexibility matters more than perfection.
- A registered dietitian should review the plan if the client has medical conditions or specific dietary requirements.

# Home Cardio Addition: 12-Week Strength Programme

**Client profile:** 27 years old, beginner, training at home
**Equipment:** Yoga mat, doorway pull-up bar, plus whatever a small flat allows (no treadmill, no bike)
**Goal:** Improve aerobic fitness and recovery capacity without compromising strength gains

---

## Principles

- Keep cardio low-to-moderate in intensity during Phase 1 and Phase 2 so it does not interfere with strength progress.
- Place cardio after strength work on training days, or on rest days as a separate session.
- Use the talk test as the main intensity guide: moderate means you can speak in short sentences; hard means only a few words at a time.
- Keep impact in check. He lives in a flat, so low-impact or quiet options should be the default, especially for neighbours below.

---

## Weekly Cardio Structure

| Phase | Weekly cardio | Format |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4) | 2 sessions of 20 min | Steady, moderate |
| Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8) | 2 sessions of 25 min, plus 1 short interval session | Steady + intervals |
| Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12) | 2 sessions of 25 min, plus 1 interval session of 20 min | Steady + intervals |

On strength days (Mon / Wed / Fri), keep cardio to 10–15 minutes at the end of the session when included. On rest days (Thu / Sat / Sun), schedule the main cardio sessions.

---

## Cardio Options (No Equipment Required)

**Low-impact steady options (Phase 1 default):**
- Brisk walking on a route outside, 20–30 minutes, ideally a hill or incline
- Stair climbing in a building stairwell, 10–15 minutes at a steady pace
- Low-impact step-touch or marching with arm movement, 20 minutes, with music
- Shadow boxing at a moderate pace, 3-minute rounds with 1-minute rests

**Interval options (Phase 2 onwards):**
- Stair sprints: 30 seconds fast up, 60–90 seconds walk down, 8 rounds
- Bodyweight circuit: 40 seconds of work, 20 seconds rest, 8 rounds, using high knees, mountain climbers, squat jumps (quiet landing), and skater hops
- Shadow boxing intervals: 30 seconds high-tempo punching, 30 seconds recovery, 10 rounds
- Hill walking intervals outdoors: 1 minute uphill brisk, 2 minutes easy, 6 rounds

**Quiet-impact swaps (if neighbours are a concern):**
- Replace jumping with step-ups, low squats, and marching variations
- Use stair climbing or cycling-style movement on the mat (slow bicycle crunch with leg movement)

---

## Sample Week (Phase 2)

- **Mon:** Strength Session A, then 10 min steady step-touch
- **Tue:** Rest or 25 min steady walk
- **Wed:** Strength Session B, then 10 min stair climbing
- **Thu:** 25 min steady walk or shadow boxing
- **Fri:** Strength Session C, then 10 min mountain climbers and marching
- **Sat:** 30 min interval session (hill walk intervals or stair sprints)
- **Sun:** Rest or mobility routine

---

## Progression and Recovery

- Increase duration by 5 minutes every two weeks within each phase, not both duration and intensity at once.
- Track resting heart rate or a perceived effort score. If he is consistently exhausted, drop one interval session and keep the steady work.
- Keep at least one full rest day per week.
- Ensure at least 48 hours between hard interval sessions and heavy leg-day strength work.

---

## Coaching Notes

- Screen for cardiovascular conditions, high blood pressure, or chest pain before starting intervals. Refer for medical clearance if any apply.
- Ask him to warm up for 5 minutes before any interval session.
- Stair work and jumping carry joint load; check knees and ankles during the first two weeks.
- Log duration, perceived effort, and any unusual breathlessness or dizziness.

Good question to get ahead of, since the programme is built around bodyweight and he'll eventually hit the ceiling of what the doorway bar and his own body can offer. Here's what I'd recommend, in priority order.

## Buy First (Under £/$100 total)

**Adjustable dumbbells or a pair of fixed dumbbells**
Start with a pair around 10–20 kg each, or an adjustable set that goes to about 20–25 kg per hand. Adjustable is better in a flat because it saves space. These cover rows, goblet squats, RDLs, lunges, presses, and carries, which is most of the gap in his programme.

**Resistance bands (a set of loop bands)**
Light to heavy loop bands are cheap, compact, and useful for assisted pull-ups, banded push-up and pull-up progressions, hip thrusts, and lateral walks. They also make a good partner for the doorway bar.

**Suspension trainer (e.g. TRX-style straps)**
These anchor to the doorway or a sturdy hook and add serious pulling and core variety. Check the door anchor is rated and the frame is solid before use. Many trainers see better returns from these than from any other single item.

## Buy Second (once he's through Phase 2)

**Kettlebell (one, around 12–16 kg for most men starting out)**
Excellent for swings, goblet squats, Turkish get-ups, and carries. One bell is enough at first. Get a second weight later if he outgrows the first.

**Ankle or wrist weights**
Optional. Dumbbells and bands do the job better and more safely in most cases.

## Probably Skip

- Barbells and racks: he doesn't have the space, and dumbbells cover most needs at this level.
- Weighted vests: useful later, but not needed in a 12-week beginner block.
- Ab wheels, gimmick trainers, and vibration plates: low value for the cost.

## Practical Notes for the Flat

- Measure the space and check the ceiling height before buying anything heavy overhead.
- Store dumbbells on a rubber mat to protect floors and reduce noise. This matters more than people expect.
- Buy from a seller with a returns policy. He may find 10 kg too light for rows within a month.
- If budget is tight, bands plus a suspension trainer will carry him through the programme. Dumbbells can come later.

If you tell me his budget and whether he has a garage or spare corner, I can narrow this to a specific shortlist.

# Phase 2 Intensity Increase: Revised Plan (Weeks 5–8)

**Goal:** Raise the challenge in Phase 2 by shifting exercises toward harder leverages, reducing rest, adding load where possible, and pushing effort closer to failure. Volume stays controlled so recovery keeps pace.

**Intensity guide:** Most working sets should finish at RPE 8–9 (1–2 reps in reserve). Week 8 includes one top set at RPE 9–10 per main lift.

---

## Core Changes to Phase 2

- **Rest periods:** Cut to 60–75 seconds on accessory work; keep 2–3 minutes on pistol and pull-up work.
- **Tempo:** Use 3-second lowering (eccentric) on all push, pull, and squat variations.
- **Load:** Add a backpack or dumbbells where available (see weight recommendations). Bodyweight alone is no longer enough by Week 6.
- **Leverage:** Move to harder variations earlier, and reduce assistance (e.g., less band support).
- **Cardio:** Interval sessions move to 30-second work intervals at higher output.

---

## Week 5
- **Session A:** Decline push-ups (feet on sofa), tempo 3-1-1, 4×8 at RPE 8–9; Pistol squat progression (box squat, 3-second lowering), 4×5 per leg; Nordic curls (kneeling, anchored), 4×4 with 3-second lowering; Hollow body hold 3×30 seconds; Pallof press with towel anchored to door, 3×10 per side
- **Session B:** Pull-ups (full range if able; otherwise 5×4 with 5-second lowering, or band-assisted if needed); Bulgarian split squat, holding dumbbells or a loaded backpack, 4×8 per leg; Single-leg RDL with dumbbell or backpack, 4×8 per leg; Feet-elevated australian rows, 4×8; Dragon flag progression (tuck to half), 3×5
- **Session C:** Diamond push-ups, 4×8 at RPE 8–9; Jump squats, 4×8 (quiet landing); Single-leg glute bridge with 3-second hold, holding a backpack, 4×10 per leg; Wall handstand hold, 3×25 seconds; Hanging leg raises, 4×8

## Week 6
Add one set to each main exercise (main = pull-ups, pistol progression, Bulgarian split squat, decline/diamond push-ups). Pull-ups progress to 5×5 if full reps are achieved at RPE 8; otherwise 5×4 with 6-second lowering. Pistol squats drop one box step lower. Add 5 kg to any loaded movement where all sets reach 10 reps with good form.

## Week 7
- **Session A:** Pseudo-planche push-ups (hands by hips), tempo 3-1-1, 5×6; Pistol squat to lower box, 4×5 per leg; Nordic curls (full or assisted), 5×4; Hollow body rocks, 3×12; Single-arm towel row, 4×10 per side
- **Session B:** Chin-ups 5×6; Wide-grip pull-ups 4×5; Shrimp squats 4×6 per leg (add goblet hold if available); Single-leg hip thrust on sofa, backpack on hips, 4×12 per leg; Front lever tuck holds 3×15 seconds; L-sit on floor between chairs 3×15 seconds
- **Session C:** Archer push-ups 4×5 per side; Jump lunges 4×10 per leg; Handstand push-up negatives against wall, 5×3 with 5-second lowering; Dead bug with hold 3×12; Hanging knee-to-elbow 4×8

## Week 8: Test and Top Sets
Retest Week 4 benchmarks plus 60-second max-rep sets of push-ups, pull-ups, and bodyweight squats. Before testing, complete one top set at RPE 9–10 on pistol squats, pull-ups, and Bulgarian split squats. Record loads, reps, and RPE for comparison with Week 4.

---

## Progression Rules

- Progress load or difficulty only when all prescribed sets reach the top of the rep range with good form and RPE 8 or below.
- If RPE is consistently 10 or form breaks down, repeat the week rather than adding difficulty.
- If joint pain increases across sessions, reduce intensity by one step, not the whole programme.

## Coaching Notes

- Confirm he has a dumbbell or backpack and a sofa or chair at the right height before Week 5. Without load, the intensity push relies entirely on leverage changes.
- Monitor sleep and soreness more closely during this block, since the intensity increase raises recovery demand. Check in midweek.
- Keep nutrition steady, but consider adding 20–30 g carbohydrate on Session B days to support the higher volume.

# Saturday Finisher Day: Fun Conditioning Add-On

**Client profile:** 27 years old, beginner, training at home
**Placement:** Saturdays, as a standalone session (replaces the Saturday interval session from the cardio plan in Phase 2 and 3, or runs in addition to it in Phase 1 if he has the energy)
**Duration:** 25–35 minutes including warm-up and cool-down
**Intensity:** Moderate to hard, finishing with fun rather than exhaustion

Saturday is a rest day in the strength plan, so this session should not add heavy leg or pulling load. Keep the work mostly conditioning and skill-based, with low-impact options as the default for flat living.

---

## Session Format

- **Warm-up (5 min):** Marching with arm swings, 10 arm circles each way, 10 bodyweight squats, 5 inchworms.
- **Main (15–20 min):** Pick one of the three formats below each week, rotating through them.
- **Finisher game (5 min):** A short challenge from the list below.
- **Cool-down (5 min):** Slow walking, hamstring and hip flexor stretches, deep breathing.

---

## Format Rotation

**Format A: Shadow Boxing Ladder**
Three-minute rounds of shadow boxing at increasing tempo. Round 1: light jab-cross. Round 2: add hooks and slips. Round 3: add bob-and-weave and footwork. Rest 60 seconds between rounds. Repeat the ladder twice.

**Format B: Stair or Hill Challenge**
Choose a stairwell or a hill route. Climb at a steady pace for 2 minutes, then walk down. Repeat 6–8 times. Count total climbs and try to beat the number next week. Skip this format if stairs cause knee or ankle pain.

**Format C: Mat Circuit Roulette**
Set a timer for 15 minutes. Each minute, do a different exercise from the list below, then rest 20 seconds at the end of the minute. Options: high knees, skater hops (quiet version: step-jumps), mountain climbers, bear crawl, burpees (step-back version), plank jacks, lateral shuffles, shadow sprints.

---

## Fun Finisher Games (pick one each week)

- **Ladder Challenge:** Ten rounds of 10 seconds on, 5 seconds off, across squat, push-up, high knees, and plank. Count total reps and beat them next Saturday.
- **Dice Workout:** Roll two dice (or use a random number app) to choose exercise and rep count. Keep it quiet and low-impact.
- **Beat the Clock:** Set a 60-second timer and complete as many mountain climbers as possible, then rest 60 seconds. Repeat for 5 rounds.
- **Partner Challenge:** If he has a friend or partner, do a shared 10-minute circuit and compete on total reps. Virtual competition works too: you can set a leaderboard and post scores.
- **Music Mix:** Build a 20-minute playlist. Shadow box or march for each song, changing move on every track change.

---

## Progression

- Add 1–2 minutes to the main format every two weeks.
- Swap one exercise for a harder variation (e.g., step-jump for jump squat) only when the current version feels comfortable.
- Keep the total session under 40 minutes so it stays recoverable.

---

## Coaching Notes

- Check in after the first two Saturdays to confirm recovery on Sunday and readiness for Monday's Session A.
- If Saturday is the day he most wants to be social or out, offer the Partner Challenge or Stair Challenge as an outdoor option.
- Keep neighbours in mind: default to low-impact options before 9am and after 8pm.
- Log score, perceived effort, and how Monday's session felt. Adjust if the finisher is interfering with strength performance.

# Mobility Routine: 12-Week Strength Programme

**Client profile:** 27 years old, beginner, training at home
**Equipment:** Yoga mat, doorway pull-up bar (optional), a sofa or chair for support
**Placement:** Daily 10 minutes on rest days (Thu, Sun), a 5-minute version after strength sessions (Mon, Wed, Fri), and a 10-minute routine on Saturdays before the finisher
**Goal:** Restore hip, thoracic, shoulder, and ankle range of motion needed for deep squats, pistols, pull-ups, and handstand work, and reduce stiffness from training.

---

## Principles

- Move slowly and breathe steadily. Mobility is controlled range, not forced stretching.
- Work to the first point of resistance, then hold or move gently within it. Mild tension is fine; sharp pain is not.
- Pair mobility with the movements it supports, so the routine doubles as practice for the strength work.

---

## Core Routine (10 minutes, rest days)

1. **Cat-cow (1 min):** 10 slow reps, exhaling as you round the spine.
2. **World's greatest stretch (2 min):** 5 reps per side. Lunge, hand to floor inside the front foot, rotate open to the ceiling.
3. **90/90 hip switches (2 min):** 5 slow switches each way, sitting on the mat with both knees at 90 degrees.
4. **Deep squat hold (2 min):** Heels down if possible, elbows pressing knees out, using a doorframe or sofa for balance. Breathe into the back.
5. **Thoracic rotations (1 min):** 8 per side, lying on the side with knees stacked, arm sweeping open.
6. **Hamstring and calf stretch (1 min):** Towel on the foot, leg straight, 30 seconds each side.
7. **Hip flexor kneeling stretch (1 min):** 30 seconds per side, squeezing the glute of the back leg.

---

## Post-Strength Routine (5 minutes, Mon / Wed / Fri)

1. **Doorway chest stretch (1 min):** Forearm on frame, step through gently.
2. **Dead hang with scapular shrugs (1 min):** Hang from the bar, 10 slow shrugs, relax.
3. **Ankle rocks (1 min):** Knee over toes against the wall, 10 per side.
4. **Child's pose with lat reach (1 min):** Hold 30 seconds each side.
5. **Hip flexor stretch (1 min):** Alternate sides, 30 seconds each.

---

## Saturday Pre-Finisher Routine (10 minutes)

- **Wall slides (2 min):** Back flat against wall, arms sliding up in a goalpost shape, 10 reps.
- **Band-free pass-throughs with towel (2 min):** Wide grip on a towel, arms overhead and behind, 8 reps.
- **Deep squat hold (2 min):** As above.
- **Pigeon pose (2 min):** 1 minute each side.
- **Cat-cow and breathing (2 min):** Slow nasal breathing, 10 reps.

---

## Progression

- **Weeks 1–4:** Hold each stretch for the times above, focus on comfort and breathing.
- **Weeks 5–8:** Add 5 seconds to each hold and introduce the pistol-prep and handstand-prep positions as active drills (e.g., controlled heel-elevated squats, wall-facing holds).
- **Weeks 9–12:** Use active mobility, such as loaded end-range holds and controlled articular rotations, before skill sessions.

---

## Coaching Notes

- Ask him to film a deep squat and overhead reach in Week 1 so you can see where range is limited.
- Stop any stretch that produces sharp, pinching, or numbness symptoms, and report it.
- If he has existing back, hip, or shoulder problems, refer to a physiotherapist before adding end-range work.
- Mobility is supplementary. If time is short, the post-strength 5-minute routine is the minimum worth keeping.

# 12-Week Strength Programme: Full Plan

**Client:** 27-year-old male, beginner, training at home
**Equipment:** Yoga mat, doorway pull-up bar, sofa or sturdy chair. From Week 5: backpack loaded with books, and dumbbells if purchased.
**Schedule:** Strength Mon / Wed / Fri. Cardio and mobility on Tue / Thu / Sun. Saturday finisher.

Before Week 1, check the doorway bar is rated for his bodyweight and mounted into the frame, and that there's clear space with no walls, furniture, or light fittings in the swing path.

---

## Weekly Template

| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| Mon | Strength A + 5-min post-strength mobility |
| Tue | Steady cardio (20–25 min) or rest |
| Wed | Strength B + 5-min post-strength mobility |
| Thu | Rest day: 10-min mobility + cardio (see phase) |
| Fri | Strength C + 5-min post-strength mobility |
| Sat | Fun finisher (25–35 min) + 10-min pre-finisher mobility |
| Sun | Rest day: 10-min mobility, optional easy walk |

**Warm-up (every strength session, 5 min):** 2 min marching or jumping jacks, 10 arm circles each way, 10 bodyweight squats, 10 scapular pull-downs on the bar, 5 inchworms.

**Rest:** 60–90 seconds between sets in Phase 1, 60–75 seconds on accessories in Phase 2, 2–3 minutes on pistol and pull-up work. Phase 3 follows the same rest, adjusted in Week 10.

**Effort guide:** Most working sets finish at RPE 8–9 from Week 5 onward. Phase 1 should finish around RPE 7–8.

---

## Phase 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–4)

**Goal:** Learn the pushing, pulling, squatting, and core patterns. Build joint readiness and baseline work capacity.

### Week 1
- **Session A:** Incline push-ups (hands on sturdy table or sofa arm) 3×8; bodyweight squats 3×12; glute bridges 3×12; dead hangs 3×15–20 s; plank 3×20 s
- **Session B:** Negative pull-ups (jump to top, lower over 4 s) 3×3; reverse lunges 3×8 per leg; wall-supported split squat hold 3×20 s per leg; superman holds 3×15 s; dead bug 3×8 per side
- **Session C:** Pike push-ups on mat 3×6; single-leg glute bridges 3×8 per leg; wall sit 3×30 s; bird dogs 3×8 per side; tuck hollow body hold 3×15 s

### Week 2
Same structure. Add 2 reps to push-ups and squats, extend hangs to 25 s, and lengthen negative pull-up lowering to 5 s.

### Week 3
- **Session A:** Standard push-ups 3×6 (or incline if not yet able); goblet-style squat holding a loaded backpack 3×12; glute bridge march 3×10 per side; dead hangs 3×25 s; plank 3×30 s
- **Session B:** Towel rows or australian rows under a sturdy table 3×8; reverse lunges 3×10 per leg; bodyweight single-leg RDL 3×8 per leg; hollow body hold 3×20 s; side plank 3×20 s per side
- **Session C:** Pike push-ups 3×8; Bulgarian split squat (rear foot on sofa) 3×8 per leg; wall sit 3×45 s; dead bug 3×10 per side; hanging knee raises 3×8

### Week 4: Deload and Benchmarks
Drop one set from each exercise, keep reps the same, and focus on form. Record these baselines for comparison at Week 8 and Week 12:
- Max standard push-ups (strict)
- Max strict pull-ups (or max negatives at 5 s if none)
- Max single-leg box squat per leg
- Plank time
- Hollow body hold time
- Max bodyweight squats in 60 s

Recalculate nutrition targets from his bodyweight trend at the end of this week.

---

## Phase 2: Build (Weeks 5–8), Intensity Push

**Goal:** Increase strength through harder leverages, slower tempos, added load, and efforts closer to failure.

**Changes from Phase 1:**
- Working sets finish at RPE 8–9 (1–2 reps in reserve)
- 3-second lowering on all push, pull, and squat variations
- Load added: backpack from Week 5, dumbbells when available
- Less assistance on pull-up and band work
- Accessory rest cut to 60–75 s; keep 2–3 min on pistol and pull-up work
- Pre-session carbohydrate increased by 20–30 g on Session B days
- Warm-up adds 5 scapular pull-ups before main work

### Week 5
- **Session A:** Decline push-ups (feet on sofa), tempo 3-1-1, 4×8; box pistol progression (3-second lowering), 4×5 per leg; kneeling Nordic curls (anchored feet), 4×4 with 3-second lowering; hollow body hold 3×30 s; Pallof press with towel anchored to door, 3×10 per side
- **Session B:** Pull-ups (full range if able; otherwise 5×4 with 5-second lowering, or band-assisted if needed); Bulgarian split squat holding backpack or dumbbells, 4×8 per leg; single-leg RDL with load, 4×8 per leg; feet-elevated australian rows, 4×8; dragon flag progression (tuck to half), 3×5
- **Session C:** Diamond push-ups, 4×8; jump squats with quiet landing, 4×8; single-leg glute bridge with 3-s hold, holding backpack, 4×10 per leg; wall handstand hold, 3×25 s; hanging leg raises, 4×8

### Week 6
Add one set to each main exercise (pull-ups, pistol progression, Bulgarian split squat, decline or diamond push-ups). Pull-ups progress to 5×5 if full reps are achieved at RPE 8; otherwise 5×4 with 6-second lowering. Drop pistol box one step lower. Add 5 kg to any loaded movement where all sets reach the top of the rep range with good form.

### Week 7
- **Session A:** Pseudo-planche push-ups (hands by hips), tempo 3-1-1, 5×6; pistol squat to lower box, 4×5 per leg; Nordic curls (full or assisted), 5×4; hollow body rocks, 3×12; single-arm towel row, 4×10 per side
- **Session B:** Chin-ups 5×6; wide-grip pull-ups 4×5; shrimp squats 4×6 per leg (add goblet hold if available); single-leg hip thrust with backpack on hips, 4×12 per leg; front lever tuck holds 3×15 s; L-sit between chairs 3×15 s
- **Session C:** Archer push-ups 4×5 per side; jump lunges 4×10 per leg; wall-supported handstand push-up negatives, 5×3 with 5-second lowering; dead bug with hold, 3×12; hanging knee-to-elbow 4×8

### Week 8: Test and Top Sets
Before testing, complete one top set at RPE 9–10 on pistol squats, pull-ups, and Bulgarian split squats. Then retest all Week 4 benchmarks plus 60-second max-rep sets of push-ups, pull-ups, and bodyweight squats. Log loads, reps, and RPE.

**Progression rule:** Advance load or difficulty only when all sets reach the top of the rep range with good form and RPE 8 or below. If RPE is consistently 10 or form breaks down, repeat the week. If joint pain increases across sessions, reduce intensity one step.

---

## Phase 3: Peak (Weeks 9–12)

**Goal:** Consolidate strength, add density and skill work, and finish with a strong test.

Keep RPE 8–9 on working sets. Load from Phase 2 carries forward.

### Week 9
- **Session A:** Standard push-ups 4×10; archer push-ups 3×6 per side; elevated pike push-ups on sofa 3×8; hollow body hold 3×40 s; plank with shoulder taps 3×20 per side
- **Session B:** Pull-ups 5×6 (or negatives if not yet able); pistol squat 3×6 per leg; Nordic curls 4×5; single-arm towel row 3×10 per side; front lever tuck holds 3×20 s
- **Session C:** Handstand push-up negatives 4×4; jump lunges 3×12; single-leg hip thrust 3×15 per leg; L-sit 3×20 s; hanging leg raises 3×12

### Week 10: Density Block
Each session becomes a circuit: complete all exercises in order, rest 90 s, repeat for 3 rounds. Aim to match or exceed Week 9 rep totals in each round.

### Week 11: Skill Emphasis
- **Session A:** Full-range pistol squats and handstand holds, 3×3, prioritising quality
- **Session B:** Pull-ups 5×5 with 2-minute rests
- **Session C:** Archer push-up and L-sit progressions, 4 sets each
- Nordic curls and hollow holds in every session

### Week 12: Final Test
Retest push-ups, strict pull-ups, pistol squats per leg, handstand hold, plank, and hollow hold. Compare with Week 4 and Week 8 and document the changes.

---

## Cardio Integration

| Phase | Rest-day cardio (Tue / Thu / Sun) | Saturday |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (Wk 1–4) | 2 × 20 min steady, moderate (talk test: short sentences) | Finisher |
| 2 (Wk 5–8) | 2 × 25 min steady, plus 1 short interval session | Finisher (intervals on Saturday replaced by finisher) |
| 3 (Wk 9–12) | 2 × 25 min steady, plus 1 interval session of 20 min | Finisher |

**Interval options:**
- Stair sprints: 30 s fast up, 60–90 s walk down, 8 rounds
- Quiet bodyweight circuit: 40 s work, 20 s rest, 8 rounds (high knees, mountain climbers, step-jumps, skater hops)
- Shadow boxing: 30 s high-tempo, 30 s recovery, 10 rounds
- Hill walking: 1 min uphill brisk, 2 min easy, 6 rounds

**Steady options:** Brisk walk on an incline (20–30 min), stair climbing (10–15 min), shadow boxing (3-min rounds, 1-min rest), low-impact step-touch with music.

Increase steady duration by 5 minutes every two weeks within a phase, but not duration and intensity together. Keep at least 48 hours between hard intervals and heavy leg work. Use low-impact options before 9am and after 8pm.

---

## Saturday Finisher

**Duration:** 25–35 minutes including warm-up and cool-down.

**Structure:** 5-min warm-up, 15–20 min main format, 5-min finisher game, 5-min cool-down.

**Rotate weekly through these formats:**
- **A: Shadow boxing ladder.** Three 3-minute rounds at rising tempo (jab-cross; add hooks and slips; add bob-and-weave and footwork). Rest 60 s between rounds. Repeat twice.
- **B: Stair or hill challenge.** Climb steadily for 2 min, walk down, repeat 6–8 times. Track total climbs. Skip if stairs cause knee or ankle pain.
- **C: Mat circuit roulette.** 15-minute timer, one exercise per minute from high knees, step-jumps, mountain climbers, bear crawl, step-back burpees, plank jacks, lateral shuffles, shadow sprints. 20 s rest at the end of each minute.

**Finisher games (pick one weekly):**
- Ladder Challenge: 10 rounds of 10 s on / 5 s off across squat, push-up, high knees, and plank. Beat the total next week.
- Dice Workout: roll dice to pick exercise and reps. Keep it quiet and low-impact.
- Beat the Clock: 60-second max mountain climbers, 60 s rest, 5 rounds.
- Partner Challenge: shared 10-min circuit, compete on total reps. Post scores to a leaderboard for remote accountability.
- Music Mix: 20-minute playlist, change move on each track.

**Progression:** Add 1–2 minutes to the main format every two weeks. Step up to harder variations only when the current one feels comfortable. Keep the session under 40 minutes.

---

## Mobility Routine

**Rest days (Thu / Sun, 10 min):**
1. Cat-cow, 10 slow reps (1 min)
2. World's greatest stretch, 5 per side (2 min)
3. 90/90 hip switches, 5 each way (2 min)
4. Deep squat hold, heels down if possible, using a doorframe for balance (2 min)
5. Thoracic rotations, 8 per side (1 min)
6. Towel hamstring and calf stretch, 30 s each side (1 min)
7. Kneeling hip flexor stretch, 30 s per side (1 min)

**Post-strength (Mon / Wed / Fri, 5 min):**
1. Doorway chest stretch (1 min)
2. Dead hang with 10 scapular shrugs (1 min)
3. Wall ankle rocks, 10 per side (1 min)
4. Child's pose with lat reach, 30 s each side (1 min)
5. Hip flexor stretch, 30 s each side (1 min)

**Saturday pre-finisher (10 min):** Wall slides, 10 reps (2 min); towel pass-throughs, 8 reps (2 min); deep squat hold (2 min); pigeon pose, 1 min per side (2 min); cat-cow with slow nasal breathing (2 min).

**Progression:** Weeks 1–4 focus on comfort and breathing. Weeks 5–8 add 5 s to holds and introduce active pistol-prep and handstand-prep drills (heel-elevated squats, wall-facing holds). Weeks 9–12 use loaded end-range holds before skill sessions.

---

## Nutrition Summary

Confirm his bodyweight, height, activity level, and any restrictions before finalising. Recalculate at Weeks 4 and 8.

**Calories:**
- Estimate BMR with Mifflin-St Jeor: (10 × kg) + (6.25 × cm) − (5 × age) + 5
- Multiply by 1.4 (desk job, 3 sessions/week) or 1.5 (lightly active)
- Target maintenance + 200–300 kcal/day for muscle gain

**Macros:**
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day, spread across 4 meals
- Fat: 25–30% of calories (not below 0.7 g/kg)
- Carbohydrates: remainder, weighted toward pre- and post-training meals (add 20–30 g on Session B days from Week 5)

**Structure:** Four meals, each with a palm-sized or larger protein portion. Pre-training snack 60–90 min before sessions (20–30 g protein, 40–60 g carbohydrate).

**Supplements:** Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g daily, after checking kidney function. Whey only if protein targets are hard to hit. Vitamin D 1,000–2,000 IU in winter or with limited sun exposure.

**Water:** About 35 ml/kg daily, plus 500 ml around each session.

**Weekly adjustment:** Weeks 1–2 log food and bodyweight daily. From Week 3, review the two-week average. If gain is under 0.25 kg/week, add 150 kcal/day. If over 0.5 kg/week, reduce by 150 kcal/day. Hold steady in Weeks 9–12 unless bodyweight shifts unexpectedly.

---

## Equipment Plan

| Timing | Item | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Week 5 | Backpack with books | Loaded squats, lunges, RDLs, hip thrusts |
| Before Week 5 if possible | Loop resistance bands | Assisted pull-ups, Pallof work, hip thrusts |
| Before Week 5 if possible | Suspension trainer | Extra pulling and core variety, anchored to a rated door hook |
| After Phase 2 | Adjustable dumbbells (around 20–25 kg per hand) | Rows, RDLs, goblet squats, presses, carries |
| Optional later | One kettlebell (12–16 kg) | Swings, get-ups, carries |

Store weights on a rubber mat to protect floors and reduce noise. Buy from a seller with a returns policy.

---

## Recovery and Lifestyle

- **Sleep:** 7–9 hours. The biggest recovery lever, and more important during the Phase 2 intensity push.
- **Soreness:** Mild soreness in the first two weeks is normal. Sharp joint pain, numbness, or worsening pain across sessions means reducing load or getting a medical check.
- **Rest:** At least one full rest day per week, and Sunday is the main one. Check in midweek during Phase 2.
- **Logging:** Reps, load, RPE (1–10), pain, sleep, and Saturday finisher scores.

---

## Coaching Checklist for the Remote Trainer

- **Week 1:** Request video of each exercise, plus a deep squat and overhead reach to identify range limits.
- **Screening:** Check shoulder, elbow, lower back, knee, ankle, and cardiovascular history before starting. Refer to a physiotherapist or doctor for pre-existing injury, high blood pressure, chest pain, or cardiovascular conditions before intervals.
- **Environment:** Confirm clear floor space, a rated doorway bar, and no fragile fittings near the swing path. Ask about neighbours below for impact decisions.
- **Week 4 and Week 8:** Record benchmarks, recalculate nutrition, and confirm equipment.
- **Week 5:** Confirm he has load (backpack or dumbbells) and a sofa or chair at the right height.
- **Ongoing:** Progress only when all sets are completed with good form and RPE 8 or below. Otherwise repeat the week.
- **Nutrition:** A registered dietitian should review if he has eating disorder history, kidney, liver, or diabetes concerns, or specific dietary needs.
- **Mobility:** Stop any stretch causing sharp, pinching, or numb symptoms. If time is short, keep the 5-minute post-strength routine as the minimum.

# 12-Week Strength Programme: Full Plan

**Client:** 27-year-old male, beginner, training at home
**Equipment:** Yoga mat, doorway pull-up bar, sofa or sturdy chair. From Week 5: backpack loaded with books, and dumbbells if purchased.
**Schedule:** Strength Mon / Wed / Fri. Cardio and mobility on Tue / Thu / Sun. Saturday finisher.

Before Week 1, check the doorway bar is rated for his bodyweight and mounted into the frame, and that there's clear space with no walls, furniture, or light fittings in the swing path.

---

## Weekly Template

| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| Mon | Strength A + 5-min post-strength mobility |
| Tue | Steady cardio (20–25 min) or rest |
| Wed | Strength B + 5-min post-strength mobility |
| Thu | Rest day: 10-min mobility + cardio (see phase) |
| Fri | Strength C + 5-min post-strength mobility |
| Sat | Fun finisher (25–35 min) + 10-min pre-finisher mobility |
| Sun | Rest day: 10-min mobility, optional easy walk |

**Warm-up (every strength session, 5 min):** 2 min marching or jumping jacks, 10 arm circles each way, 10 bodyweight squats, 10 scapular pull-downs on the bar, 5 inchworms.

**Rest:** 60–90 seconds between sets in Phase 1, 60–75 seconds on accessories in Phase 2, 2–3 minutes on pistol and pull-up work. Phase 3 follows the same rest, adjusted in Week 10.

**Effort guide:** Most working sets finish at RPE 8–9 from Week 5 onward. Phase 1 should finish around RPE 7–8.

---

## Phase 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–4)

**Goal:** Learn the pushing, pulling, squatting, and core patterns. Build joint readiness and baseline work capacity.

### Week 1
- **Session A:** Incline push-ups (hands on sturdy table or sofa arm) 3×8; bodyweight squats 3×12; glute bridges 3×12; dead hangs 3×15–20 s; plank 3×20 s
- **Session B:** Negative pull-ups (jump to top, lower over 4 s) 3×3; reverse lunges 3×8 per leg; wall-supported split squat hold 3×20 s per leg; superman holds 3×15 s; dead bug 3×8 per side
- **Session C:** Pike push-ups on mat 3×6; single-leg glute bridges 3×8 per leg; wall sit 3×30 s; bird dogs 3×8 per side; tuck hollow body hold 3×15 s

### Week 2
Same structure. Add 2 reps to push-ups and squats, extend hangs to 25 s, and lengthen negative pull-up lowering to 5 s.

### Week 3
- **Session A:** Standard push-ups 3×6 (or incline if not yet able); goblet-style squat holding a loaded backpack 3×12; glute bridge march 3×10 per side; dead hangs 3×25 s; plank 3×30 s
- **Session B:** Towel rows or australian rows under a sturdy table 3×8; reverse lunges 3×10 per leg; bodyweight single-leg RDL 3×8 per leg; hollow body hold 3×20 s; side plank 3×20 s per side
- **Session C:** Pike push-ups 3×8; Bulgarian split squat (rear foot on sofa) 3×8 per leg; wall sit 3×45 s; dead bug 3×10 per side; hanging knee raises 3×8

### Week 4: Deload and Benchmarks
Drop one set from each exercise, keep reps the same, and focus on form. Record these baselines for comparison at Week 8 and Week 12:
- Max standard push-ups (strict)
- Max strict pull-ups (or max negatives at 5 s if none)
- Max single-leg box squat per leg
- Plank time
- Hollow body hold time
- Max bodyweight squats in 60 s

Recalculate nutrition targets from his bodyweight trend at the end of this week.

---

## Phase 2: Build (Weeks 5–8), Intensity Push

**Goal:** Increase strength through harder leverages, slower tempos, added load, and efforts closer to failure.

**Changes from Phase 1:**
- Working sets finish at RPE 8–9 (1–2 reps in reserve)
- 3-second lowering on all push, pull, and squat variations
- Load added: backpack from Week 5, dumbbells when available
- Less assistance on pull-up and band work
- Accessory rest cut to 60–75 s; keep 2–3 min on pistol and pull-up work
- Pre-session carbohydrate increased by 20–30 g on Session B days
- Warm-up adds 5 scapular pull-ups before main work

### Week 5
- **Session A:** Decline push-ups (feet on sofa), tempo 3-1-1, 4×8; box pistol progression (3-second lowering), 4×5 per leg; kneeling Nordic curls (anchored feet), 4×4 with 3-second lowering; hollow body hold 3×30 s; Pallof press with towel anchored to door, 3×10 per side
- **Session B:** Pull-ups (full range if able; otherwise 5×4 with 5-second lowering, or band-assisted if needed); Bulgarian split squat holding backpack or dumbbells, 4×8 per leg; single-leg RDL with load, 4×8 per leg; feet-elevated australian rows, 4×8; dragon flag progression (tuck to half), 3×5
- **Session C:** Diamond push-ups, 4×8; jump squats with quiet landing, 4×8; single-leg glute bridge with 3-s hold, holding backpack, 4×10 per leg; wall handstand hold, 3×25 s; hanging leg raises, 4×8

### Week 6
Add one set to each main exercise (pull-ups, pistol progression, Bulgarian split squat, decline or diamond push-ups). Pull-ups progress to 5×5 if full reps are achieved at RPE 8; otherwise 5×4 with 6-second lowering. Drop pistol box one step lower. Add 5 kg to any loaded movement where all sets reach the top of the rep range with good form.

### Week 7
- **Session A:** Pseudo-planche push-ups (hands by hips), tempo 3-1-1, 5×6; pistol squat to lower box, 4×5 per leg; Nordic curls (full or assisted), 5×4; hollow body rocks, 3×12; single-arm towel row, 4×10 per side
- **Session B:** Chin-ups 5×6; wide-grip pull-ups 4×5; shrimp squats 4×6 per leg (add goblet hold if available); single-leg hip thrust with backpack on hips, 4×12 per leg; front lever tuck holds 3×15 s; L-sit between chairs 3×15 s
- **Session C:** Archer push-ups 4×5 per side; jump lunges 4×10 per leg; wall-supported handstand push-up negatives, 5×3 with 5-second lowering; dead bug with hold, 3×12; hanging knee-to-elbow 4×8

### Week 8: Test and Top Sets
Before testing, complete one top set at RPE 9–10 on pistol squats, pull-ups, and Bulgarian split squats. Then retest all Week 4 benchmarks plus 60-second max-rep sets of push-ups, pull-ups, and bodyweight squats. Log loads, reps, and RPE.

**Progression rule:** Advance load or difficulty only when all sets reach the top of the rep range with good form and RPE 8 or below. If RPE is consistently 10 or form breaks down, repeat the week. If joint pain increases across sessions, reduce intensity one step.

## Phase 3: Peak (Weeks 9–12)

**Goal:** Consolidate strength, add density and skill work, and finish with a strong test.

Keep RPE 8–9 on working sets. Load from Phase 2 carries forward.

### Week 9
- **Session A:** Standard push-ups 4×10; archer push-ups 3×6 per side; elevated pike push-ups on sofa 3×8; hollow body hold 3×40 s; plank with shoulder taps 3×20 per side
- **Session B:** Pull-ups 5×6 (or negatives if not yet able); pistol squat 3×6 per leg; Nordic curls 4×5; single-arm towel row 3×10 per side; front lever tuck holds 3×20 s
- **Session C:** Handstand push-up negatives 4×4; jump lunges 3×12; single-leg hip thrust 3×15 per leg; L-sit 3×20 s; hanging leg raises 3×12

### Week 10: Density Block
Each session becomes a circuit: complete all exercises in order, rest 90 s, repeat for 3 rounds. Aim to match or exceed Week 9 rep totals in each round.

### Week 11: Skill Emphasis
- **Session A:** Full-range pistol squats and handstand holds, 3×3, prioritising quality
- **Session B:** Pull-ups 5×5 with 2-minute rests
- **Session C:** Archer push-up and L-sit progressions, 4 sets each
- Nordic curls and hollow holds in every session

### Week 12: Final Test
Retest push-ups, strict pull-ups, pistol squats per leg, handstand hold, plank, and hollow hold. Compare with Week 4 and Week 8 and document the changes.

## Cardio Integration

| Phase | Rest-day cardio (Tue / Thu / Sun) | Saturday |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (Wk 1–4) | 2 × 20 min steady, moderate (talk test: short sentences) | Finisher |
| 2 (Wk 5–8) | 2 × 25 min steady, plus 1 short interval session | Finisher (intervals on Saturday replaced by finisher) |
| 3 (Wk 9–12) | 2 × 25 min steady, plus 1 interval session of 20 min | Finisher |

**Interval options:**
- Stair sprints: 30 s fast up, 60–90 s walk down, 8 rounds
- Quiet bodyweight circuit: 40 s work, 20 s rest, 8 rounds (high knees, mountain climbers, step-jumps, skater hops)
- Shadow boxing: 30 s high-tempo, 30 s recovery, 10 rounds
- Hill walking: 1 min uphill brisk, 2 min easy, 6 rounds

**Steady options:** Brisk walk on an incline (20–30 min), stair climbing (10–15 min), shadow boxing (3-min rounds, 1-min rest), low-impact step-touch with music.

Increase steady duration by 5 minutes every two weeks within a phase, but not duration and intensity together. Keep at least 48 hours between hard intervals and heavy leg work. Use low-impact options before 9am and after 8pm.

## Saturday Finisher

**Duration:** 25–35 minutes including warm-up and cool-down.

**Structure:** 5-min warm-up, 15–20 min main format, 5-min finisher game, 5-min cool-down.

**Rotate weekly through these formats:**
- **A: Shadow boxing ladder.** Three 3-minute rounds at rising tempo (jab-cross; add hooks and slips; add bob-and-weave and footwork). Rest 60 s between rounds. Repeat twice.
- **B: Stair or hill challenge.** Climb steadily for 2 min, walk down, repeat 6–8 times. Track total climbs. Skip if stairs cause knee or ankle pain.
- **C: Mat circuit roulette.** 15-minute timer, one exercise per minute from high knees, step-jumps, mountain climbers, bear crawl, step-back burpees, plank jacks, lateral shuffles, shadow sprints. 20 s rest at the end of each minute.

**Finisher games (pick one weekly):**
- Ladder Challenge: 10 rounds of 10 s on / 5 s off across squat, push-up, high knees, and plank. Beat the total next week.
- Dice Workout: roll dice to pick exercise and reps. Keep it quiet and low-impact.
- Beat the Clock: 60-second max mountain climbers, 60 s rest, 5 rounds.
- Partner Challenge: shared 10-min circuit, compete on total reps. Post scores to a leaderboard for remote accountability.
- Music Mix: 20-minute playlist, change move on each track.

**Progression:** Add 1–2 minutes to the main format every two weeks. Step up to harder variations only when the current one feels comfortable. Keep the session under 40 minutes.

## Nutrition Summary

Confirm his bodyweight, height, activity level, and any restrictions before finalising. Recalculate at Weeks 4 and 8.

**Calories:**
- Estimate BMR with Mifflin-St Jeor: (10 × kg) + (6.25 × cm) − (5 × age) + 5
- Multiply by 1.4 (desk job, 3 sessions/week) or 1.5 (lightly active)
- Target maintenance + 200–300 kcal/day for muscle gain

**Macros:**
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day, spread across 4 meals
- Fat: 25–30% of calories (not below 0.7 g/kg)
- Carbohydrates: remainder, weighted toward pre- and post-training meals (add 20–30 g on Session B days from Week 5)

**Structure:** Four meals, each with a palm-sized or larger protein portion. Pre-training snack 60–90 min before sessions (20–30 g protein, 40–60 g carbohydrate).

**Supplements:** Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g daily, after checking kidney function. Whey only if protein targets are hard to hit. Vitamin D 1,000–2,000 IU in winter or with limited sun exposure.

**Water:** About 35 ml/kg daily, plus 500 ml around each session.

**Weekly adjustment:** Weeks 1–2 log food and bodyweight daily. From Week 3, review the two-week average. If gain is under 0.25 kg/week, add 150 kcal/day. If over 0.5 kg/week, reduce by 150 kcal/day. Hold steady in Weeks 9–12 unless bodyweight shifts unexpectedly.

## Recovery and Lifestyle

- **Sleep:** 7–9 hours. The biggest recovery lever, and more important during the Phase 2 intensity push.
- **Soreness:** Mild soreness in the first two weeks is normal. Sharp joint pain, numbness, or worsening pain across sessions means reducing load or getting a medical check.
- **Rest:** At least one full rest day per week, and Sunday is the main one. Check in midweek during Phase 2.
- **Logging:** Reps, load, RPE (1–10), pain, sleep, and Saturday finisher scores.

## Coaching Checklist for the Remote Trainer

- **Week 1:** Request video of each exercise, plus a deep squat and overhead reach to identify range limits.
- **Screening:** Check shoulder, elbow, lower back, knee, ankle, and cardiovascular history before starting. Refer to a physiotherapist or doctor for pre-existing injury, high blood pressure, chest pain, or cardiovascular conditions before intervals.
- **Environment:** Confirm clear floor space, a rated doorway bar, and no fragile fittings near the swing path. Ask about neighbours below for impact decisions.
- **Week 4 and Week 8:** Record benchmarks, recalculate nutrition, and confirm equipment.
- **Week 5:** Confirm he has load (backpack or dumbbells) and a sofa or chair at the right height.
- **Ongoing:** Progress only when all sets are completed with good form and RPE 8 or below. Otherwise repeat the week.
- **Nutrition:** A registered dietitian should review if he has eating disorder history, kidney, liver, or diabetes concerns, or specific dietary needs.
- **Mobility:** Stop any stretch causing sharp, pinching, or numb symptoms. If time is short, keep the 5-minute post-strength routine as the minimum.
